question: What are search agents?
answer: Search agents are novel, LLM-driven search models that simulate an automated search and result understanding process to provide users with answers that are readily comprehensible and accurate [page 5, section "2.1 IR"]. These agents are conceptualized as intelligent agents that adopt a pattern mimicking human browsing and can autonomously search, interpret, and synthesize information from various sources, thereby enhancing their capacity for complex retrieval tasks [page 30, section "7 Search Agent"]; [page 35, section "8.5 Search Agent"]. WebGPT is noted as a pioneering example in this field, modeling the search process as a sequence of actions performed by an LLM-based agent within a search engine environment, thereby autonomously completing the entire search pipeline [page 5, section "2.1 IR"].

sources.quote: Though the aspect of static search agents has been thoroughly studied, the literature on dynamic search agents remains limited.

WebGPT [176] serves as a pioneering work in this category, which models the search process as a sequence of actions of an LLM-based agent within a search engine environment, autonomously accomplishing the whole search pipeline.
